subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should `subscriptionAuthDispatch` plus the shared plugin runtime eligibility helper be the permanent contract for subscription-scoped embedded runs that must execute through a CLI backend?
rationale: The behavior fix is technically supported, but adding permanent plugin/runtime API surface and choosing its ownership is a compatibility decision that tests and contributor proof cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve provider-owned seam
options.body: Keep the capability on `CliBackendPlugin`, retain per-run opt-in, and expose the shared eligibility helper as documented in this PR.

options.title: Reshape before merge
options.body: Preserve the proven behavior but replace these new contracts with the runtime owner's preferred generic helper-routing API.

options.title: Fold into broader routing work
options.body: Pause this PR and carry the active-memory fix through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57326 if maintainers want one unified helper-dispatch design.

recommendation.title: Approve provider-owned seam
recommendation.body: Keep the capability on `CliBackendPlugin`, retain per-run opt-in, and expose the shared eligibility helper as documented in this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion identifies this person as the likely runtime owner for the permanent dispatch-boundary contract.
